names.note: Read out of doxologia.ro's line for 7 mai, «Sfântul Mucenic Acachie».
Read out of saint.gr's line for 7 Μαΐου, «Άγιος Ακάκιος», with the rank word left off.

Read out of the Охридски пролог's heading for 7. мај ст. ст., „Свети мученик Акакије.“ Свети is no rank and мученик is the `martyr` this folder already carries in `types` and `honorific.js` composes back, so stripping them leaves the bare forename and nothing else: the heading gives no epithet, no rank of office, no city and no company, and the officer's commission, Maximian, Perinthus and Byzantium are all in the body. Two other folders already hold this bare form and the fold was measured before drafting, not discovered by the gate.

attestations.note: Not checked: days.pravoslavie.ru for the corresponding Julian day (24 September 2026).

source.text: Calendarul zilei, Doxologia (doxologia.ro), 7 mai — «Sfântul Mucenic Acachie»
saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 7ης Μαΐου — «Άγιος Ακάκιος»

attestations.note: The life page heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 7 Μαΐου εκάστου έτους», the same day the Romanian calendar keeps him, and it is the same soldier martyr: a man in the ranks under Diocletian's colleague, tried by one official after another at Byzantium and beheaded. **The Greek adds everything the folder lacked**: Cappadocia as his country, the end of the third century and the persecution under Galerius Maximian, whose reign it prints as 286–305; the muster at which his commander examined the soldiers to find out how many and which of them were Christians; the names of the three who tried him — the centurion Φήρμος, the proconsul Βιβιανός, and then Φαλακιανός, also spelled Φυλακιανός on the page — the flogging and the darkest prison in Byzantium, the beheading, and his age of twenty-five; and the synaxis in the quarter of Heptaskalon, in a church raised by the emperor Justinian. **One thing on this page reads against the folder's own English name.** The folder is called Acacius the Centurion, and saint.gr makes the centurion somebody else: «Ο Άγιος Ακάκιος υπηρετούσε στις στρατιωτικές τάξεις, και είχε διοικητή τον εκατόνταρχο Φήρμο» — he served in the military ranks and had the centurion Firmus for his commander. The display name is not changed by this upgrade, and the reading is recorded here and in the report. **No `dates` are added**: the page gives a reign and a century and no year of his own, and his age at death is not a date. No hymn is printed for him.

source.text: Православни подсетник (pravoslavno.rs), Охридски пролог за 20.05.2026 (7. мај ст. ст.) — „Свети мученик Акакије.“

attestations.note: **The day is Julian 7 May, the same menologion day the Romanian and the Greek keep him on, and this is the first account of him this corpus has read** — doxologia gives «Sfântul Mucenic Acachie» and no life, and saint.gr «Άγιος Ακάκιος» and no more. The identification is day, rank and the soldiering: „официр римски“ against this folder's own `soldier` and the English name it was given, the Centurion. **He is not `acacius-the-new-of-neochorion`, nor any of the other thirteen Acacii this corpus keeps** — checked by listing them all; the fourteen stand apart by day and see. **A FIRST DATE**: „Чесно пострада и пресели се у царство вечне радости 303. године.“ → `death` 303, where this folder held no `dates` at all; `node .tmp/dd.mjs "303"` reads it in both packs. New besides, and all of it new: that he was **a Roman officer in the time of the emperor Maximian**; that answering at his trial he said he had **inherited the pious faith from his own parents** and had been confirmed in it **by seeing many wonderful healings from the relics of Christian saints**; that the great torments he bore bravely were **in the Thracian city of Perinthus**; and that he was then **taken over into Byzantium**, where he endured fresh torments until he was at last beheaded with the sword. **No `locations` were taken** for Perinthus or Byzantium: he was tortured in one and died in the other, and „he was taken to Byzantium“ is not a birthplace or a see. `types` was not touched: мученик is the `martyr` the folder already holds, and the officer is its `soldier`. **One deliberate fold, a widening**: the heading's bare Акакије joins the gate's existing `? "акакије"` pair, and the row is in this batch's commit message. The Prologue prints no troparion and no kontakion.

hymns.text: Mucenicul Tău, Doamne, Acachie, întru nevoinţa sa, cununa nesctricăciunii a dobândit de la Tine, Dumnezeul nostru; că având puterea Ta, pe chinuitori a învins; zdrobit-a şi ale demonilor neputincioase îndrăzniri. Pentru rugăciunile lui, mântuieşte sufletele noastre, Hristoase Dumnezeule.

english.text: Thy martyr Acacius, O Lord, in his struggle received from thee, our God, the crown of incorruption; for having thy strength he overcame the torturers and broke the powerless daring of the demons. By his prayers save our souls, O Christ God.

death.note: Охридски пролог за 7. мај ст. ст.: „Чесно пострада и пресели се у царство вечне радости 303. године.“ — the book prints the year plainly and this folder held no date at all before it; doxologia and saint.gr both give him a bare line with no century. `node .tmp/dd.mjs "303"` reads it in both packs. No year of birth is printed anywhere.
